name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,768

entries.clue: Respected English horse touring Middle East (8)

indicatorNotes.touring: a traveller touring a region goes all round it, so the horse wraps round the Middle East

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a steed is a horse, split STEE…D round the next piece
ME is the usual abbreviation for the Middle East

annotation.surface: A well-regarded English racehorse on a tour of the Gulf states.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Respected English horse' reads as one noun phrase, but the definition stops after the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who are esteemed are held in high regard.

entries.clue: Manager charged with change, Harlow's ending season last in table (6,12)

indicatorNotes.charged with: something charged with a load carries it, so W takes ALTER on board after it
indicatorNotes.ending: a word's ending is its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of Harlow
to alter is to change
one of the four seasons
the team last in a league table is bottom

annotation.surface: A football manager charged with turning round a club from Harlow, a town in Essex, that finished the season bottom of the league.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charged with' tempts you to read W for 'with'; in fact it is Harlow's ending that gets loaded with the change.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Walter Winterbottom was England's first national football manager, from 1946 to 1962.

entries.clue: Sound clear and brilliant inside skull — is this needed? (7,3)

annotation.definition: Sound clear and brilliant inside skull — is this needed?

indicatorNotes.inside: what is inside the skull sits within the letters of HEAD

blocks.note: a bell rings when it sounds clear
A1 = first-rate, with the 1 read as I
the skull is the head, split HEA…D round the rest

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether they need help to make sound ring clear and bright in their head.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. A1 written AI is a common crossword trick.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks whether you need a device to make sound clear inside your head, which is exactly what a hearing aid does.

entries.clue: See 2
More safe crackers triggering alarm? (8)

indicatorNotes.crackers: crackers means crazy, and crazy letters do not stay in order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Safe-crackers who set off the burglar alarm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Safe crackers' reads as one phrase about burglars; split it after 'safe' and 'crackers' becomes the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Something fearsome frightens people, so it is triggering alarm in them.

entries.clue: Neptunian feature regularly seen that spews lava (4)

annotation.definition: feature regularly seen that spews lava
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is 'feature … that spews lava' with 'regularly seen' as the indicator in the middle

indicatorNotes.regularly seen: letters seen at regular intervals are every other one

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters: nEpTuNiAn

annotation.surface: An astronomer describes a volcanic feature spotted again and again on Neptune.
annotation.walkthrough: Neptune is a red herring: the volcano is in Sicily, and the 'feature' is read with the words around the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Etna, on Sicily, is Europe's most active volcano, a landscape feature that erupts lava.

entries.clue: World's response where Conservative rises (8)

indicatorNotes.rises: in a down entry, something that rises moves towards the top, so C goes first

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a reaction is a response; lift its C out, leaving REATION

annotation.surface: A commentator reports how the world reacted when the Conservatives surged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'World's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is 'is': World is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by sense: creation is everything that was created, the whole world.

entries.clue: See 2
Room tiny arachnid enters backwards — it has four dimensions (5-4)

indicatorNotes.enters: to enter a room is to go inside it
indicatorNotes.backwards: the arachnid's letters run the other way

blocks.note: room and space both mean extent to move in, split SPAC…E
a mite is a tiny eight-legged creature

annotation.surface: A mite creeps into a room, followed by a note that the room has four dimensions.
annotation.walkthrough: Three dimensions of space plus one of time make the four; ordinary rooms have only three.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: in relativity, space-time is one continuum of three space dimensions and one of time.

entries.clue: Strange sort of force leaving dismembered body (5)

indicatorNotes.Strange: strange means out of the ordinary, so SORT comes out of its usual order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
'of' with F (force, the physics symbol) removed

annotation.surface: A detective sees a strange kind of force at work in the remains of a dismembered body.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sort of force' looks like a physics term; the force is only an F to be taken out of 'of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a torso is the trunk left when a body has lost its head and limbs.

entries.clue: Metallica finally exiting festival compound (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally in Metallica is its last letter
indicatorNotes.exiting: a letter exiting a word goes out of it, so the A leaves

blocks.note: the Christian spring festival
last letter of Metallica, removed from EASTER

annotation.surface: The heavy metal band Metallica pulls out of a music festival at the last minute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Festival' looks like a rock festival; it is the church one.
annotation.definitionFit: A chemistry sense: an ester is a compound formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol.

entries.clue: Brawling woman to call Turkish leader, not without guts (9)

indicatorNotes.without guts: a gutted word has lost its insides, so NOT keeps only N and T

blocks.note: to term something is to call it that
an aga was an Ottoman commander
NOT emptied

annotation.surface: A pugnacious woman refuses to address a Turkish chief as anything but gutless.
annotation.walkthrough: AGA, an Ottoman title, is a crossword staple for 'Turkish leader'.
annotation.definitionFit: Termagant was once a supposed Muslim deity played as a ranting tyrant in medieval plays, and the name passed to any violent, quarrelsome woman.

entries.clue: Sailor runs into sea, extremely eager (7)

indicatorNotes.into: running into the sea puts the runs inside it
indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea, split MA…IN
R = runs, the cricket scoring abbreviation
first and last letters of eager

annotation.surface: An eager sailor dashes into the waves.
annotation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the high seas, as in the Spanish Main.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mariner, from Latin mare 'sea', is a formal word for a seafarer.

entries.clue: Mansion rebuilt for personal pleasure (7)

indicatorNotes.rebuilt: a rebuilt house is put together again differently, and so are the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A rich owner remodels a stately home just to please themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Personal pleasure' sounds like a hobby; it is a coy euphemism.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism: onanism is masturbation, pleasure a person gives themselves.

entries.clue: Supremely evil influence in Chartist reforms (10)

indicatorNotes.reforms: to re-form something is to shape it anew, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A historian blames a wicked influence for the Chartists' reform programme.
annotation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 19th-century British movement for voting reform, which is why 'reforms' fits the surface. 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: In Christian belief the Antichrist is Christ's great adversary, the embodiment of evil at the end of days.

entries.clue: American rotter holding Henry back in Russian cottage (5)

indicatorNotes.holding: the American rotter holds Henry inside
indicatorNotes.back: going back means reading the letters from the end

blocks.note: A = American
H = henry, the unit of inductance
a cad is a dishonourable man

annotation.surface: An American scoundrel keeps a man named Henry captive in a Russian country house.
annotation.walkthrough: Henry is the unit of inductance, not a man; the whole string is turned round at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A loanword: dacha is the Russian word for a country house or summer cottage outside a city.

entries.clue: Dish with seafood: chicken to follow (8)

blocks.note: a cock is a male chicken
to tail someone is to follow them

annotation.surface: A menu: a seafood starter, with chicken as the main course.
annotation.walkthrough: A prawn cocktail is a classic British starter of prawns in a pink sauce.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a seafood cocktail, such as prawn cocktail, is shellfish served cold in a sauce.

entries.clue: Proper contest shortened (3)

indicatorNotes.shortened: a shortened word loses its tail, here the final L

blocks.note: a duel is a contest between two, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A proper contest cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proper contest' reads as one phrase; the first word alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in use: 'with due care' means with proper care, what is fitting.

entries.clue: Kid arrested by police inspector, put away for attack (8)

indicatorNotes.arrested by: someone arrested is held, so RIB is held inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector
to put food away is to eat it, split AT…E
to kid or rib is to tease

annotation.surface: A youngster is arrested by a detective and jailed for assault.
annotation.walkthrough: Kid is the verb 'tease', not a child, and put away means eaten, not jailed.
annotation.definitionFit: A verbal sense: a diatribe is a bitter spoken or written attack.

entries.clue: End of sunbathing? Make tracks for dance (5)

blocks.note: a tan is the end product of sunbathing
to make tracks is to leave

annotation.surface: Sunbathing over, it is time to head off to a dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of sunbathing' looks like a last letter, G; the question mark says it is the end in the sense of result.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tango, from Buenos Aires, is one kind of ballroom dance.

entries.clue: Insider from Acton wrongly claiming prize (8)

indicatorNotes.wrongly: letters put wrongly are out of their right order
indicatorNotes.claiming: to claim a prize is to take it in, so the anagram takes CUP inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder, split OC…ANT round CUP
a trophy cup is a prize

annotation.surface: An insider from Acton, a district of west London, falsely claims a prize.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a hidden-word or source instruction but is only surface glue for the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning synonym: an occupant is literally someone inside a building or vehicle.

entries.clue: Atlantic Provinces bordering right rural idyll (7)

indicatorNotes.bordering: the provinces lie on both borders of the R, so they wrap round it

blocks.note: Acadia was the French colony in what are now Canada's Maritime provinces, split A…CADIA
R = right

annotation.surface: Canada's Atlantic seaboard presented as an unspoilt countryside paradise.
annotation.walkthrough: Acadia is the historical name for the French lands of Canada's Atlantic coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary sense: Arcadia, a region of Greece, stands in pastoral poetry for an idyllic countryside.

entries.clue: Cold in HGV in polar region (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the cold is sitting in the lorry, so C goes inside its letters

blocks.note: an HGV (heavy goods vehicle) is a lorry; an artic is an articulated one, split AR…TIC
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A lorry driver feels the cold in a polar landscape.
annotation.walkthrough: Artic is British slang for an articulated lorry.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name by description: the Arctic is the region round the North Pole.

entries.clue: Short French article perhaps coming to a point? (7)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: perhaps flags an example, and LA is one of several French articles

blocks.note: la is French for 'the', feminine
a cone comes to a point

annotation.surface: A short article in French that gets straight to the point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short … coming to a point' sounds like one description of terse writing; the question mark marks the playful reading of CONIC.
annotation.definitionFit: The Spartans of Laconia were famous for curt speech, so laconic means short in words.

entries.clue: Secure gold in horse-drawn carriage (6)

blocks.note: to land a deal is to secure it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Bullion being shipped safely in a horse-drawn coach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but is a link word; the pieces sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the landau, named after the German town of Landau, is a four-wheeled carriage with a folding top.

entries.clue: Drink downed noisily at bar after opening (6)

indicatorNotes.noisily: said noisily means said out loud, so we take the sound of the word
indicatorNotes.after opening: only the letters of bar after its first

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to down it
bar without its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone gulps a drink loudly at the pub bar as soon as it opens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is British slang for drinking fast.
annotation.definitionFit: In myth nectar is the drink of the gods, and by extension any delicious drink.

entries.clue: Vessel crossing river in southwest — atomic boat (9)

indicatorNotes.crossing: a vessel crossing a river spans it, so CAN reaches round the river

blocks.note: a can is a metal container, split CA…N
the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in England's southwest
A = atomic, as in A-bomb

annotation.surface: A ship steams across a river in the West Country, followed by a nuclear-powered boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like the definition for a boat; it is the container, and the boat comes last.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a catamaran is a boat with twin parallel hulls.

entries.clue: Sheep's flesh not being cooked for dog (4)

indicatorNotes.not being cooked: food being cooked is 'on'; not so, ON goes

blocks.note: mutton is the meat of a sheep, less ON

annotation.surface: Raw mutton handed to the dog.
annotation.walkthrough: Food on the stove is 'on', so meat that is not being cooked loses ON.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal usage: mutt is a slangy word for a dog, especially a mongrel.

entries.clue: State main points again where MP bans duke (5)

indicatorNotes.bans: to ban someone is to keep them out, so D is kept out of the word

blocks.note: a redcap is a British military policeman, from the red cap band
D = duke, removed

annotation.surface: A summary of a debate where a Member of Parliament shuts out a duke.
annotation.walkthrough: MP looks like Member of Parliament; it is Military Police, whose British nickname is redcaps.
annotation.definitionFit: Recap is short for recapitulate, to go over the main points once more.

entries.clue: Tees had the ne plus ultra, ensnaring old fool (5)

indicatorNotes.ensnaring: a snare traps its prey inside, so the ultimate traps the old

blocks.note: Tees is the setter, so 'Tees had' is I'D
the ultimate is 'it', split I…T
O = old

annotation.surface: The setter boasts of having the very best, except that it trapped an old fool.
annotation.walkthrough: Ne plus ultra is Latin for 'nothing further', the ultimate; that is 'it', as in 'this is it'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: idiot, from Greek for a private, ignorant person, now just means a fool.

entries.clue: Seaman stole this empty wagon (9)

indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word has lost its contents, so THIS keeps only T and S

blocks.note: a boa is a feathery stole
THIS emptied
a wain is an old farm wagon

annotation.surface: A sailor stole this cart after emptying it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as a verb, the seaman's theft; it is the noun, a scarf-like wrap.
annotation.definitionFit: A rank by type: the boatswain, or bosun, is the ship's officer in charge of crew and rigging.
